Telecom Customer Support Knowledge Base Support procedures for broadband mobile billing accounts and installation This manual provides practical guidance for telecom support agents. Equipment-specific instructions, contractual entitlements, identity-verification requirements and financial adjustments must follow the applicable approved procedure. It does not establish new customer charges, credit limits, restoration guarantees or regulatory requirements.

Contents Chapter 1 Fiber Broadband Gateways and Wi-Fi Troubleshooting Chapter 2 Mobile Services SIM and Porting Procedures Chapter 3 Billing Audits Portal Access and Security Chapter 4 Home Installation and Technician Dispatch Final Agent Checklist Technical References

Chapter 1 Fiber Broadband Gateways and Wi-Fi Troubleshooting 1.1 Understand the equipment The Optical Network Terminal, or ONT, connects the premises to the fibre access network. The gateway or router connects that service to local wired and wireless devices. Some installations combine functions in one unit.

A healthy optical connection does not by itself establish that authentication, addressing, routing or Wi-Fi is working.

1.2 Read ONT lights correctly Identify the exact manufacturer and model before interpreting colours. Some devices have separate Power, PON and LOS indicators; others use a combined Optical light.

The following patterns illustrate common Openreach equipment, not a universal chart for every ONT. [1] Power light showing Green On the referenced ONT models, equipment has power. Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

Power light showing Off On the referenced ONT models, check the accessible approved power connection and supply. Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

PON light showing Solid green On the referenced ONT models, optical registration is established. Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

PON light showing Flashing with LOS off On the referenced ONT models, registration or verification may be in progress. Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

PON light showing Off On the referenced ONT models, optical connection or registration needs investigation. Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

LOS light showing Red or flashing red On the referenced ONT models, this pattern commonly indicates an optical alarm; confirm the model's meaning.

Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

LAN or Port light showing On On the referenced ONT models, ethernet link is detected. Confirm the exact model guide before taking action.

1.3 Safe power and physical checks

1. Ask whether the ONT and gateway are powered.

2. Check accessible connections to the supplied, approved adapters.

3. Ask about recent furniture movement, drilling, building work or power interruptions.

4. Request a safe visual observation of the cable route.

5. Look for reported crushing, sharp bends, pulling, visible damage or water exposure.

1.4 WAN port and Ethernet checks The gateway's WAN port connects it to the upstream service. Its LAN ports connect local devices.

1. Confirm which ONT Ethernet port is provisioned.

2. Confirm that its lead reaches the gateway's designated WAN port.

3. Check the link indicators at both ends.

4. With consent, reseat only accessible Ethernet connectors.

5. Test a known-good compatible Ethernet lead where available.

6. Check supported negotiated link speed and errors.

If optical registration is healthy but Ethernet link is absent, investigate the lead, supported port and equipment before assuming a fibre-line fault.

1.6 Wi-Fi dead zones Walls, metal objects, interference and equipment placement can reduce wireless performance. Wireless bands also differ in their reach and sensitivity to obstacles. [2]

1. Compare service near the gateway with the affected location.

2. Test another compatible device.

3. Check whether the issue is weak coverage, interference or a device-specific fault.

4. Place the gateway in an open, suitable location.

5. Avoid enclosed cupboards, metal barriers and unnecessary obstruction.

6. Review supported band and channel settings.

7. Retest where the customer actually uses the service.

Do not promise full coverage in every room without an assessment.

1.7 Mesh puck placement A satellite needs a reliable connection to the main mesh unit. Placing it deep inside the existing dead zone may leave it with poor backhaul.

1. Confirm that the main unit works normally.

1.8 Router overheating Restricted ventilation and direct sunlight can contribute to overheating and degraded operation. [4] Ask whether the gateway is:

• Covered or enclosed.

• Stacked against other hot equipment.

• Exposed to direct sunlight.

• Restarting or becoming unresponsive.

For equipment without a safety warning, follow approved guidance to improve ventilation and observe stability.

Warmth alone does not establish hardware failure.

For a burning smell, smoke, deformation or electrical damage, stop ordinary troubleshooting and arrange the designated safety response.

1.11 Restart versus factory reset A restart and a factory reset are different actions.

• Restart temporarily interrupts operation.

• Factory reset may erase customised or required settings.

A factory reset is not the default response to disconnections. Use it only when the approved procedure requires it, consent is obtained, and the supported restoration method is confirmed.

1. Review the current plan and documented change terms.

2. Confirm whether immediate or next-cycle fulfilment is eligible.

3. Preview the applicable billing treatment.

4. Explain charges and credits separately.

5. Obtain explicit acceptance.

6. Process the eligible order.

7. Confirm the effective date and next-bill explanation.

Chapter 3 Billing Audits Portal Access and Security 3.1 Auditing an itemised bill

1. Verify the account holder or authorised representative.

2. Identify the disputed amount and period.

3. Compare current and previous statements.

4. Review accepted orders and effective dates.

5. Separate recurring charges, usage, equipment, one-time fees, taxes and adjustments.

6. Check payment allocation and carried-forward balances.

7. Compare relevant usage and consent records.

8. Determine whether the charge is valid, erroneous or still under investigation.

9. Explain the evidence and next action.

A higher bill is not automatically an incorrect bill. Conversely, an unfamiliar charge should not be dismissed without checking its basis.

3.2 Roaming fee disputes A customer describing roaming as accidental does not automatically establish refund entitlement.

1. Review the applicable plan and destination coverage.

2. Check the recorded network, timestamps and chargeable usage.

3. Investigate possible rating errors, unsupported charges or disputed consent.

4. Explain verified findings in plain language.

5. Reverse a confirmed error only through authorised billing controls.

3.3 Courtesy credits A courtesy credit is a discretionary service-recovery decision, separate from correcting an erroneous charge or applying a documented entitlement.

Before issuing one:

• Confirm eligibility.

• Check the agent's approval authority.

• Review previous relevant adjustments.

• State the proposed amount and reason accurately.

• Obtain required approval.

• Record whether it is pending or posted.

Never invent a standard credit amount, promise approval in advance or state that a credit has reached the bill before verifying it.

Openreach's installation guidance illustrates the importance of permissions, access, power and an agreed cable route. Provider-specific attendance requirements must be checked separately. [11] 4.2 Drop-cable entry The technician must assess the route. An agent should not prescribe drilling, excavation or physical construction instructions to an unqualified customer.

The authorised route should account for:

1. Required access and permissions.

2. Existing utilities and structural restrictions.

3. Manufacturer-specified fibre handling and bend limits.

4. Protection against crushing, pulling and exposure.

5. Applicable sealing and fire-safety requirements.

6. The agreed internal termination location.

Where additional work is needed, explain the verified prerequisite and planning owner. Do not keep booking standard visits for a site that is not ready.

4.3 ONT wall mounting Installation must follow the exact equipment instructions and applicable site requirements.

Qualified technicians should:

• Use an approved mounting arrangement and suitable surface.

• Maintain specified orientation and ventilation clearances.

• Avoid locations exposed to water, damaging heat or impact.

• Provide supported accessible power.

• Protect the fibre route without sharp bends or strain.

• Leave access for authorised maintenance.

• Agree a practical router connection and placement.

Do not invent a universal mounting height, screw type, fibre bend radius or clearance. Those values depend on the model and installation specification.

Customers should not detach, relocate or remount an installed ONT themselves.

4.4 Installation completion Before recording completion:

1. Confirm the authorised physical work is finished.

2. Verify equipment registration and service provisioning.

3. Check the optical and Ethernet states.

4. Test the supported customer connection.

5. Explain power, routine restart and support arrangements.

6. Identify any remaining defect or incomplete item.

7. Record the accepted handover.

5. Share only verified milestones with the customer.

Do not pressure a technician to override a safety assessment.
